# Conformance against R

This is the layer-2 number from [ADR
0005](decisions/0005-conformance-and-verification.md): the **Porffor
discipline**, where the R interpreter itself is the ground-truth oracle.

A generator emits programs over the in-subset grammar (`R/tccq_conformance.R`).
Each program is compiled by `tccq` **and** evaluated by R on several random
inputs, and the results are diffed (numeric tolerance, NA/NaN positions must
match). The generator only emits constructs that are `core` in the
[grammar coverage map](r-subset-grammar.md), so the contract is exact:

> **passed == total, always.** A drop is a real regression, and the gating test
> `inst/tinytest/test_tccq_conformance.R` fails CI.

```{r}
cf <- tccq_conformance_run(n_cases = 40L)
```

## Result

**`r cf$passed` / `r cf$total`** generated programs match the R interpreter
(seed `20260611`, 4 random inputs each, TinyCC backend).

```{r}
by_status <- table(factor(cf$results$status, levels = c("pass", "fail", "error")))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(by_status, responseName = "count"),
             col.names = c("status", "count"), row.names = FALSE)
```

A sample of the generated programs:

```{r}
set.seed(1)
sample_rows <- cf$results[sort(sample(nrow(cf$results), min(10L, nrow(cf$results)))), c("expr", "status")]
names(sample_rows) <- c("Generated program", "Status")
knitr::kable(sample_rows, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Bounded-exhaustive check

Random sampling can miss cases. The harness also runs a **bounded-exhaustive**
pass: every depth-1 elementwise kernel (a leaf, a unary op of a leaf, or a binary
op of two leaves, over `{x, y, 1, 2}`) is compiled and diffed against R. This is
*complete* up to depth 1, not merely sampled.

```{r}
ex <- tccq_conformance_enumerate()
```

**`r ex$passed` / `r ex$total`** depth-1 elementwise kernels match the R
interpreter.

## Growing the suite

This generated corpus is the seed. Per ADR 0005 it grows by (1) widening the
generator as the `core` surface grows, (2) deepening the bounded-exhaustive pass,
and (3) harvesting in-subset fragments from `r-svn/tests/` (`arith.R`,
`any-all.R`, `primitives.R`). The number only goes up as coverage widens; it must
never drop for a fixed seed.
